pages.title: Read the situation

pages.author: Scenario briefing · fictional
pages.subject: Should phones be banned at school?
paragraphs: Fictional school discussion, not a research finding: social-message checking interrupts lessons. Consider three uses separately: social notifications, an approved accessibility tool, and urgent family contact. No policy outcome is claimed to be universal. The group must agree a purpose, a restriction and a private exception route.

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: What problem should a school phone policy actually solve?
lines.audioText: What problem should a school phone policy actually solve?
lines.translation: Que problema uma política de celular na escola deveria resolver?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: For this case, repeated social-message checking is interrupting lessons
lines.audioText: For this case, repeated social-message checking is interrupting lessons.
lines.translation: Neste caso, a consulta repetida de mensagens sociais está interrompendo as aulas

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Then a total ban might be simpler than many exceptions
lines.audioText: Then a total ban might be simpler than many exceptions.
lines.translation: Então uma proibição total poderia ser mais simples do que muitas exceções

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Possibly, although some learners use a phone as an accessibility tool
lines.audioText: Possibly, although some learners use a phone as an accessibility tool.
lines.translation: Talvez, embora alguns alunos usem o celular como recurso de acessibilidade

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Could the rule allow approved tools while restricting social notifications?
lines.audioText: Could the rule allow approved tools while restricting social notifications?
lines.translation: A regra poderia permitir recursos aprovados e restringir notificações sociais?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: That seems more targeted. We’d need a clear way to request an exception without public explanations
lines.audioText: That seems more targeted. We’d need a clear way to request an exception without public explanations.
lines.translation: Parece mais direcionado. Precisaríamos de um jeito claro de pedir exceção sem explicações públicas

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: What about family contact during an emergency?
lines.audioText: What about family contact during an emergency?
lines.translation: E contato com a família durante uma emergência?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: A named contact route could help, but we shouldn’t assume the current office system is always fast enough
lines.audioText: A named contact route could help, but we shouldn’t assume the current office system is always fast enough.
lines.translation: Um canal definido poderia ajudar, mas não devemos presumir que a secretaria atual é sempre rápida o bastante

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: So the policy needs a rule, a reason and a workable exception process
lines.audioText: So the policy needs a rule, a reason and a workable exception process.
lines.translation: Então a política precisa de regra, motivo e processo viável de exceção

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes. Whereas distraction is the target, some phone use supports participation
lines.audioText: Yes. Whereas distraction is the target, some phone use supports participation.
lines.translation: Sim. Enquanto a distração é o alvo, alguns usos apoiam a participação

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: I’d test the draft against concrete cases before saying it treats everyone fairly
lines.audioText: I’d test the draft against concrete cases before saying it treats everyone fairly.
lines.translation: Eu testaria o rascunho com casos concretos antes de dizer que trata todos de forma justa

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Agreed. Despite the need for consistency, identical treatment isn’t always the right response
lines.audioText: Agreed. Despite the need for consistency, identical treatment isn’t always the right response.
lines.translation: Concordo. Apesar da necessidade de consistência, tratamento idêntico nem sempre é a resposta adequada

pages.title: Define the policy’s purpose

pages.title: Build contrast clauses with although and despite
pages.instruction: Concede a point while keeping the grammatical form of the connector clear

rows.subject: Concession with a clause
rows.example: Although phones can distract, some uses help pupils participate

rows.subject: Concession with a noun or -ing
rows.verb: despite / in spite of + noun phrase / verb-ing
rows.example: Despite the interruptions, some phone use is necessary

rows.subject: Contrast two situations
rows.example: Social notifications interrupt, whereas a reading tool can help

pages.note: Although takes a full clause; despite does not normally take one directly. To follow despite with a clause, use despite the fact that. Despite has no of.

pages.title: Role-play the situation
pages.instruction: Design a workable policy. Agree on a policy and test it with a real-life case

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: An accessibility case was omitted. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. There’s a case our draft policy hasn’t addressed. A learner uses a phone to read material aloud and communicate when speaking is difficult. Asking for permission publicly every lesson would draw attention to private information and could delay participation. The learner isn’t asking to use social media. Could you reconsider how the exception works, rather than treating this as a choice between no rules and unlimited phone use? A private agreement, clear permitted use and a way to review problems might be worth discussing. The main classroom concern remains repeated social-message checking, so we still need a rule that addresses that specific problem
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. There’s a case our draft policy hasn’t addressed. A learner uses a phone to read material aloud and communicate when speaking is difficult. Asking for permission publicly every lesson would draw attention to private information and could delay participation. The learner isn’t asking to use social media. Could you reconsider how the exception works, rather than treating this as a choice between no rules and unlimited phone use? A private agreement, clear permitted use and a way to review problems might be worth discussing. The main classroom concern remains repeated social-message checking, so we still need a rule that addresses that specific problem.

pages.title: Respond to the message
pages.instruction: Revise one condition, not the whole purpose. Test the exception process and revise one condition without changing the policy’s purpose

pages.title: One rule, different needs
pages.instruction: Compare two school phone policies, then propose a rule and one clear exception

video.title: Phones are not the problem — Channel 4 News

items.prompt: How do the schools’ rules differ at break and lunchtime?
items.hint: Compare “not seen or heard” with the student’s description of breaks
items.answer: The headteacher’s school keeps phones out of sight. The student’s school allows them at breaks, but not during lessons

items.prompt: Why can a phone distract someone even when it is not being used?
items.hint: Listen for buzzing and wondering what a notification could be
items.answer: The student says the buzzing and the thought of what might be on the phone can keep distracting students, even when they are not actively using it

items.prompt: Why does the headteacher think device restrictions are not enough?
items.hint: Contrast the phone itself with the content and apps available on it
items.answer: He thinks the policy is well meant, but harmful content, apps and the businesses distributing them are a bigger problem

items.prompt: Propose a phone rule and one exception. What is the trade-off?
items.hint: Use although or whereas. You may consider an approved learning or medical use; those are your proposed cases
items.answer: Example: Although notifications can distract, a student could use an approved medical app with staff agreement. Other phones would stay silent and out of sight. We would need a clear way to approve the exception fairly
